summary: Orbit Forge is a browser-based, pixel-art educational game that teaches space mission design through hands-on systems engineering. Space missions require balancing competing demands—budget, mass, power, data, communications, and time—where upgrading one subsystem impacts every other. Designed for students, teens, and aspiring engineers, Orbit Forge lets players assemble spacecraft, validate launch vehicle and orbit compatibility in real time, navigate branching in-flight anomalies, and analyze detailed post-mission reports explaining why their mission succeeded or failed
details:
What It Does & How It Works: Orbit Forge turns abstract space mission trade-offs into an interactive, progressive game loop:

  1. Scenarios & Mission Briefing: Players choose from multiple mission scenarios (such as Earth Observation, Moon, and Mars), each featuring 5 progressively challenging missions with strict resource budgets and objectives.
  2. Spacecraft & Orbit Assembly: Players select a launch vehicle, spacecraft platform, scientific instruments, power systems, communications, and target orbit. A live validation engine checks mass-to-orbit limits, power balance, budget, and downlink capacity, providing plain-language explanations for any design conflict.
  3. In-Flight Branching Decisions & Tasks: During flight, players respond to incoming transmissions (e.g., solar storms, power dips, communication blackouts) via two-choice branching trees that dynamically alter resources and mission outcomes, followed by destination-specific task execution.
  4. Post-Mission Analysis: Every run ends with a comprehensive debrief showing resource usage, star rating, and plain-language root-cause explanations ("WHY?" learning cards) for any failure.

Tech Stack & Current Status: Built with Next.js (static export), JavaScript, Tailwind CSS (custom pixel-art design system), Motion, and GSAP for flight choreography, powered by static JSON datasets and localStorage for instant, account-free browser play.

  • Currently Working: Full gameplay loop across scenarios, real-time 6-resource HUD, live launch vehicle/orbit compatibility validator, interactive tutorials library, and local progress saving.
  • Limitations & Future Plans: Currently single-player with static datasets; planned additions include 4-player role-based team mode, sandbox mode, cloud saves, and Arabic localization.
